$comment: Security is modelled as a set of independent toggles. A 'level' is just a preset that switches a group of them on, so you can pick a level and then adjust anything individually.

levels.name: Relaxed
levels.desc: Stock NixOS defaults. The firewall is on and nothing else gets in your way.
levels.bestFor: Single-user desktops that never expose a port to the internet.

levels.name: Baseline
levels.desc: Sensible hygiene for a machine that other people can reach. Key-only SSH, brute-force protection, tighter sudo.
levels.bestFor: Home servers, VPS boxes, anything with SSH open.

levels.name: Hardened
levels.desc: Kernel and userspace hardening on top of the baseline. Some observability tools and debuggers stop working.
levels.bestFor: Internet-facing servers and workstations holding sensitive data.

levels.name: Paranoid
levels.desc: Hardened kernel, module locking, SMT disabled, device control and auditing. This will break things - read every warning.
levels.bestFor: Threat models where you would rather lose a feature than lose the machine.

toggles.name: Firewall
toggles.desc: Deny all inbound traffic except the ports your selected services need.

toggles.name: SSH: keys only, no root
toggles.desc: Disable password and keyboard-interactive login, and refuse direct root logins.
toggles.warn: Add your public key under users.users.<name>.openssh.authorizedKeys.keys before you reboot, or you will lock yourself out.

toggles.name: fail2ban
toggles.desc: Ban IP addresses that repeatedly fail authentication.

toggles.name: Restrict sudo to wheel
toggles.desc: Only members of the wheel group may run sudo at all.

toggles.name: Use doas instead of sudo
toggles.desc: Replace sudo with OpenBSD's doas, which has a far smaller attack surface.
toggles.warn: Scripts and tooling that shell out to `sudo` will stop working unless you keep a compatibility alias.
nix: extraRules = [{ groups = [ "wheel" ]; keepEnv = true; persist = true; }];

toggles.name: Restrict the Nix daemon
toggles.desc: Only wheel members may talk to the Nix daemon and build derivations.

toggles.name: AppArmor
toggles.desc: Load AppArmor mandatory access control profiles at boot.

toggles.name: Kernel sysctl hardening
toggles.desc: Hide kernel pointers and dmesg, restrict ptrace, and turn on the usual network anti-spoofing knobs.
toggles.warn: ptrace_scope = 1 stops debuggers attaching to processes you did not start. Game anti-cheat and some profilers dislike this.

toggles.name: Protect the kernel image
toggles.desc: Prevent replacing the running kernel and disable hibernation.
toggles.warn: Hibernation (suspend-to-disk) stops working. Suspend-to-RAM is unaffected.

toggles.name: Lock kernel modules
toggles.desc: Refuse to load any kernel module after boot has finished.
toggles.warn: Hot-plugged hardware that needs a module not loaded during boot will not work. VirtualBox, some VPNs and external GPUs break.

toggles.name: Disable core dumps
toggles.desc: Stop the kernel writing process memory to disk when something crashes.

toggles.name: Blacklist obscure network protocols
toggles.desc: Refuse to load DCCP, SCTP, RDS, TIPC and other rarely used protocol modules.

toggles.name: Blacklist legacy filesystems
toggles.desc: Refuse to load cramfs, freevxfs, jffs2, hfs, udf and friends.
toggles.warn: Blacklisting udf stops optical media mounting, and squashfs is not blacklisted here precisely because AppImage and snap need it.

toggles.name: Hardened kernel
toggles.desc: Build on the linux-hardened patch set with stricter defaults throughout.
toggles.warn: Incompatible with the proprietary NVIDIA driver, ZFS and VirtualBox, and measurably slower. Do not use this on a gaming machine.

toggles.name: Disable SMT / Hyper-Threading
toggles.desc: Mitigates the whole family of cross-thread side-channel attacks.
toggles.warn: You lose roughly a third of your multi-threaded CPU performance.

toggles.name: USBGuard
toggles.desc: Block USB devices that were not present at boot until you explicitly allow them.
toggles.warn: Configured here to allow already-connected devices so you do not lose your keyboard. Newly plugged devices are blocked until authorised with `usbguard allow-device`.

toggles.name: Firejail
toggles.desc: Namespace sandbox for individual applications.

toggles.name: Audit daemon
toggles.desc: Log every execve system call to the kernel audit log.
toggles.warn: Produces a lot of log volume on a busy machine.

toggles.name: DNS over TLS
toggles.desc: Resolve names through systemd-resolved with DNSSEC and encrypted transport.
toggles.warn: Captive portals on public wifi often fail until you temporarily relax this.

toggles.name: Randomise wifi MAC
toggles.desc: Present a different hardware address to every network you join.
toggles.warn: Networks that authorise you by MAC address, and some captive portals, will stop recognising the machine.

toggles.name: ClamAV
toggles.desc: On-demand virus scanner with an auto-updating signature database.

toggles.name: OpenSnitch
toggles.desc: Interactive outbound application firewall - prompts when a program phones home.
toggles.warn: The daemon only. Run the opensnitch-ui package in your desktop session to get the prompts.

toggles.name: Automatic upgrades
toggles.desc: Rebuild nightly against the channel or flake so security fixes land without you.
toggles.warn: Unattended upgrades can pull in a broken package. Keep allowReboot off unless the machine is genuinely disposable.
